title: Art. 52 - Principio de probidad administrativa
summary: The article's metadata is largely correct; the only concrete gap is the empty `sanctions` list, which should record the administrative liability the article itself attaches to a breach of the probity principle.

suggestions.rationale: The article itself states that breach of the probity principle entails the responsibilities and sanctions set by the Constitution, the laws and paragraph 4 of the Title, which maps to administrative liability.
suggestions.justification: Article 52, third paragraph, expressly provides that inobservance of the probity principle 'acarreará las responsabilidades y sanciones que determinen la Constitución, las leyes y el párrafo 4° de este Título'. The vocabulary rule maps 'acarreará responsabilidades' to `administrative_liability`. Because the consequence is attached by this very article, it is not a sanction described only elsewhere. The reference to paragraph 4 does not make the consequence purely disciplinary, so the broader administrative liability token is the safest fit.
suggestions.evidence: Su inobservancia acarreará las responsabilidades y sanciones que determinen la Constitución, las leyes y el párrafo 4° de este Título, en su caso.

decision_logic.sanctions: Scan the article's own text for consequence language ('acarreará', 'será sancionado', 'incurrirá en'); map 'acarreará responsabilidades' to administrative_liability; do not infer sanctions from the instrument's topic or from other articles.
decision_logic.norm_type: Keep existing tokens when the article states a general principle and imposes a duty on named subjects; do not add facets not explicitly present.
decision_logic.scope: Keep existing tokens when the addressees are the public administration and its officials and the domain is administrative law.
decision_logic.direction: Keep 'mandatory' where the operative verb is 'deberán'.
decision_logic.doc_type: Leave as 'unknown' because the snippet does not supply a controlled doc_type token.
